components.name: alacritty_terminal

maintenance.statusAtReview: Official Alacritty project; emulator in production use for years

runtimeSecurity.notes: The crate ships a tty module capable of spawning processes, but Kinein never calls it; sessions are created by portable-pty and only raw bytes reach the emulator.

components.name: rustix
components.role: Safe `access(2)` for the `serial` domain: tells whether the user can read and write a serial device node WITHOUT opening it (opening asserts DTR/RTS on most USB-UART bridges and resets the board)
components.integration: Rust crate linked only by kinein-core, one call site in serial.rs (`rustix::fs::access`). Declared with default-features = false and features ["std", "fs"]. Chosen over a stat()-based check because access(2) honours POSIX ACLs, which is how udev's TAG+="uaccess" grants the seat user access without any group; a mode-bit heuristic would report `root:dialout 0660` as writable for a user outside dialout, or as denied for a user covered by the ACL.

version.reason: Already resolved at 1.1.4 in Cargo.lock as a transitive dependency of portable-pty (rustix-openpty) and alacritty_terminal (polling) before this adoption; declaring it directly adds no crate and no second version.

license.spdx: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT
license.source: crates.io version metadata for 1.1.4, read on 2026-09-11; MIT and Apache-2.0 are already in deny.toml

maintenance.statusAtReview: Active: Bytecode Alliance project, latest release 2026-02-22; it is the syscall layer under std-adjacent crates such as tempfile and the async-io stack.

runtimeSecurity.notes: It is a thin wrapper over Linux syscalls (raw syscalls or libc, chosen by the crate's backend); the `unsafe` lives inside it and none in this repository (#![forbid(unsafe_code)] stays). Kinein calls only fs::access, which reads nothing and writes nothing.

cost.notes: Measured with `cargo tree -i rustix` on 2026-09-11: the crate was already in the graph via polling and rustix-openpty; the direct declaration only widens its feature set by `fs`.

components.verification: cargo deny check (advisories, bans, licenses, sources) green on the real workspace with the crate declared, 2026-09-11; the `serial` tests exercise access() against 0o000, 0o060 and 0o600 nodes

version.reason: Safe high-level API for SQLConnect, bounded row buffers and standard catalog cursors; no repository unsafe/FFI code.

components.name: tokio-postgres / tokio / futures-util
components.role: Streaming PostgreSQL transaction preview inside the existing job worker
components.integration: Published Rust crates linked by kinein-core; one current-thread runtime only for the preview job. The IPC dispatcher and Core::new do not require an application runtime. Configuration and verified TLS are shared with synchronous operations.

version.pin: Existing Cargo.lock versions/checksums; direct workspace constraints 0.7, 1 and 0.3
version.reason: Already transitive dependencies of existing database drivers. Direct declarations enable simple_query_raw streaming and one-use decision channels; no new crate or resolved version was added.

license.source: Published manifests installed in Cargo registry; tokio is MIT, tokio-postgres and futures-util are MIT OR Apache-2.0. Existing deny policy unchanged.

maintenance.statusAtReview: Pinned published releases from the official rust-postgres, Tokio and Rust futures projects. APIs and licenses checked against the resolved local sources; this entry makes no claim that they are the latest upstream versions.

runtimeSecurity.notes: SQL and credentials go only to the selected PostgreSQL endpoint, as in the existing driver. No telemetry or unrelated content upload. Credential/configuration objects stay in the worker; driver allocations do not guarantee zeroization of every internal copy.

cost.notes: Cargo.lock changes only the three dependency names in kinein-core. No permanent runtime, pool or extra process. Limits apply to retained samples, not every driver frame allocation. Hostname resolution uses the Tokio blocking pool; runtime Drop may wait beyond the connect future timeout if system DNS/NSS stalls. Preview capacity stays held; the lifecycle correction is required in roadmap 59 section 7 before closure.

scopeControls: Typed public context checked before credentials and jobs; production/read-only policy remains active
Up to four live previews per core, one per workspace/profile name; capacity held through finalization
Connection and transaction owned by the worker; registry stores only public context and one-use decision channel
Shared verified TLS configuration requires TLS and never falls back to plaintext
15 s total query budget, 60 s decision, 12 s finalize; server statement/lock/idle transaction limits
128 columns, 16 KiB cells, 8 MiB retained sample, bounded maxRows; stream drains all rows and retains NULL
Context loss cancels pending decisions; accepted COMMIT is not revocable and lost replies are reported as unknown
verification: Unit tests for strict params, lexer/RETURNING, capacity, expiry, one-use decisions, revoked context and TLS mode
QML stale context, cancel, expiry, accepted decision and unknown outcome harness
Real PostgreSQL commit/rollback, deferred constraint refusal, lock/expiry/retention limits and FATAL/EOF during COMMIT
Cargo deny plus complete Rust/C++/QML gates and MSRV 1.88 --locked
